source.notes: A CISCE item bank of 75 competency-focused practice questions for ISC Class XI Biotechnology (not an examination paper). The cover prints 'ISC Competency Focused Practice Questions, Biotechnology, Class - XI', 'First edition: August 2026'; the preface is signed by the Chief Executive & Secretary, 31st August 2026. PDF pages 1-5 are cover, copyright, mission, preface and contents; printed page N is PDF page N+5. Questions are on printed pages 1-28 (PDF 6-33), the Answer Key on printed pages 29-37 (PDF 34-42), so answerSourceUrl equals sourceUrl. Marks come from the section headings: I MCQ (1 mark each, Q1-16), II Assertion-Reason (1 mark each, Q17-21), III Very Short Answer (1 mark each, Q22-35), IV Short Answer (2 marks each, Q36-54), V Long Answer (3 marks each, Q55-65), VI Very Long Answer (4 marks each, Q66-75); total 146. Sub-parts print [1] each, consistent with the section marks; each question is kept as one entry and the sub-part marks brackets are omitted from the text. No maximum marks or duration is printed. The printed topic tag (e.g. [Cell Biology - Mitosis – process]) is omitted from the text; the printed cognitive tag is recorded in cognitiveLevel only when all parts of an entry share one tag. The file name on cisce.org is spelt 'Biotechnoogy-XI.pdf'. The preface states the Answer Key 'presents the possible answers to a given question, but it is neither limiting nor exhaustive'; answers are copied verbatim and not extended. Some key entries look questionable and are reproduced as printed for editor review (e.g. Q51 '(b) To kill the germs that exist at high temperature' for rapid cooling; Q22 'Cytoplasm'; Q43(a)). Immune-system and plant-defence questions are mapped to the 'Biomolecules, Separation Techniques and Defence Strategies' chapter. Figures are not reproduced; questions that need them are flagged.

questions.text:
The diagram below shows the response of plant tissue culture to Cytokinin and Auxin. Study the diagram and answer the questions that follow:

(b) In the context of plant tissue culture, explain why the ratio of Auxin to Cytokinin a critical factor is in determining whether roots or shoots will be induced from a callus.

questions.text:
An industrial zone houses two distinct biotechnology plants. Plant A specializes in the production of high-quality probiotic yogurt and curd using Lactobacillus cultures. Plant B is a large-scale brewery producing craft beer using specific strains of Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Both plants utilize fermentation, but their factory floors look very different.
In Plant B, a byproduct is released during fermentation that causes the "fizz" in the beverage. Identify this byproduct and explain why it is not typically observed in the final product of Plant A.

officialAnswer.text: • The byproduct is carbon dioxide. It causes the fizz in beer during yeast fermentation. • It is not typically observed in yogurt or curd because Lactobacillus performs lactic acid fermentation and does not produce carbon dioxide.

questions.text:
Gracy washed her woollen sweater in hot water and noticed that it shrank after drying, whereas Trina’s silk gown remained unchanged under the same conditions.
(a) Why did the woollen sweater shrink?
(b) Why did the silk gown remain unaffected?
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Understand, (b) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The woollen sweater shrank because heat caused denaturation and tightening of wool protein fibres. (b) The silk gown remained unaffected because silk proteins are more resistant to heat-induced shrinking under these conditions.

questions.text:

(a) Calculate the expected number of green and wrinkled seeds.
(b) Compare observed and expected results.
extractionIssues: Figure on page 18 (dihybrid cross) not reproduced
Printed topic tag reads 'Introduction to Biotechnology - Mendel’s laws'; mapped to genetics

officialAnswer.text: (a) Expected green and wrinkled seeds: (1/16) x 640 = 40 (b) Observed seeds = 50; expected seeds = 40 Observed number is 10 more than the expected number, likely due to random variation.

questions.text:
Sanika and her research group were studying the catalytic activity of an enzyme E that converts substrate S into product P. During the experiment, they observed that the reaction proceeded rapidly when only the substrate was present. However, upon adding another molecule “Y”, the rate of product formation decreased sharply. Further investigation revealed that Y had a molecular structure similar to S and was competing with the substrate for the same active site on the enzyme.
(a) Identify the type of inhibition caused by molecule Y and name the molecule Y.
(b) Suggest one method by which the enzyme can favour binding of S over Y and justify your answer.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The inhibition is competitive inhibition and molecule Y is a competitive inhibitor. (b) Increase substrate concentration, as S can outcompete Y for the active site.

questions.text:
Aastha, a curious biology student at a school, was performing Mendel’s classic monohybrid cross experiment in her school laboratory. She carefully selected a true-breeding tall pea plant (TT) and crossed it with a true-breeding dwarf plant (tt). As expected, all the F₁ generation plants grew tall, which initially made her believe that the dwarf trait had completely disappeared. However, when she allowed the F₁ plants to self-pollinate and observed the F₂ generation, she was surprised to find that a few plants were dwarf again. This unexpected reappearance made her question how a trait that seemed to vanish in one generation could return in the next.
(a) Why did dwarf plants reappear in the F₂ generation despite being absent in F₁?
(b) Identify and explain the Mendelian law involved using proper genetic reasoning.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Dwarf plants reappeared because the recessive allele (t) was masked in F₁ but segregated during gamete formation, producing tt plants in F₂. (b) This follows Mendel’s Law of Segregation.

questions.text:
Observe the given figure carefully and answer the questions that follow:
During training at a brewery in Lucknow, Anantha Biswas is shown a graph depicting the activity of enzymes (amylase and protease) at different temperatures during mashing. The graph shows a peak at around 60°C, with activity decreasing sharply beyond 70°C.
(a) Identify the temperature range where enzyme activity is maximum. Explain why this range is optimal for mashing.
(b) The graph shows a steep decline in enzyme activity beyond 70°C. Explain the biochemical reason for this decline.
extractionIssues: Graph on page 20 (enzyme activity against temperature) not reproduced (its key features are described in the text)

officialAnswer.text: (a) Enzyme activity is maximum around 60°C. At this temperature amylase and protease work efficiently to break down starch and proteins respectively. (b) Beyond 70°C, enzymes get denatured.

questions.text:
Advancement in the field of nanobiotechnology and its applications to the field of medicines and pharmaceuticals has revolutionised the twentieth century.
(a) Suggest one medical application of nanobiotechnology.
(b) Explain one advantage of using nanoparticles for drug delivery over conventional chemotherapy.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Nanobiotechnology is used in targeted drug delivery for cancer treatment. (b) Nanoparticles deliver drugs specifically to diseased cells, reducing damage to healthy cells.

questions.text:
During a microbiology practical, Avanti cultured two bacterial sample A and sample B on a nutrient medium containing the antibiotic streptomycin. After incubation, colony A showed normal growth, whereas colony B did not grow. Her teacher explained that the difference in their cell wall structure influenced their response to the antibiotic.
(a) Identify which colony is most likely to represent a Gram-negative bacterium and which represents a Gram-positive bacterium.
(b) Explain why the Gram – negative bacterium is more likely to survive in the presence of streptomycin than the Gram – positive bacterium.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Understanding, (b) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Colony A represents Gram-negative bacterium, Colony B represents Gram-positive bacterium. (b) Gram – negative bacteria possess an outer membrane that acts as an additional permeability barrier, reducing the entry of streptomycin and making them relatively more resistant than Gram – positive bacteria, which lack this outer membrane.

questions.text:

(a) State which right of the plant breeder is involved in this situation.
(b) State which right of the farmer applies in this case.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Plant Breeder’s Right (b) Farmer’s Right

questions.text:
Given below is a very well-known process performed in dairy industry.
(a) What is the purpose of heating milk?
(b) Why is rapid cooling necessary after heating?

officialAnswer.text: (a) To kill the germs that exist at low temperature. (b) To kill the germs that exist at high temperature.

questions.text:
During a microscopic study of specialised cells, Fredrick observed that Cell A contained numerous membrane channels studded with ribosomes and was actively involved in synthesising digestive enzymes. In contrast, Cell B lacked ribosomes on its membrane network and was found to participate in lipid synthesis and detoxification of harmful substances.
(a) Identify the type of endoplasmic reticulum predominantly present in Cell A and Cell B.
(b) Explain how the structural differences in these organelles are related to their specific functions.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Cell A – Rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) Cell B – Smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) (b) RER has ribosomes for protein synthesis, while SER lacks ribosomes and helps in lipid synthesis and detoxification.

questions.text:
Observe the flowchart carefully and answer the questions that follow:
(a) Differentiate between lactic acid fermentation and alcoholic fermentation on the basis of:
(i) Microorganism involved
(ii) Industrial Application
(b) Explain why fermentation is considered a biological process rather than merely a chemical reaction.
extractionIssues: Flowchart on page 22 not reproduced
Table in the official answer (page 37) flattened row by row with ' | '

officialAnswer.text: (a) Refer the table: | Lactic acid fermentation | Alcoholic fermentation; Microorganism | Lactobacillus | Saccharomyces; Industrial Application | Dairy Industry | Breed/ Brewing Industry (b) Fermentation is a biological process because it is carried out by living microorganisms using enzymes to break down sugars under anaerobic conditions.

questions.text:
After recovering from chickenpox in childhood, Rohan was exposed to the same virus again years later but did not develop severe symptoms. His doctor explained that this rapid protection was due to a specific type of immunity developed during the first infection.
(a) Identify the type of immunity responsible for the faster response during the second exposure.
(b) Explain how vaccination uses the same principle to protect the body against diseases.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The type of immunity responsible is active acquired immunity. (b) Through vaccination weakened or dead pathogens are introduced into the body. This stimulates the immune system to produce memory cells, which provide a rapid and stronger response during future infections.

questions.text:
Before transferring plant explants into sterile culture tubes, a laboratory technician switched on the Laminar Air Flow (LAF) chamber and sterilised the working area with alcohol.
(a) What is the purpose of using the LAF chamber?
(b) Explain the role of HEPA filters in maintaining sterility.
(c) State two precautions to be followed while working inside the chamber.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The LAF chamber provides a sterile working environment by supplying clean, filtered air and preventing contamination during tissue culture work. (b) HEPA filters remove dust particles and microorganisms from the air, thereby maintaining sterile conditions inside the chamber. (c) Two precautions: 1. Sterilise the working area and instruments before use. 2. Do not keep culture tubes open unnecessarily to avoid contamination.

questions.text:
Researchers studying hormonal control in animal cells observed that a steroid hormone easily crossed the plasma membrane and directly entered the nucleus, where it activated genes responsible for protein synthesis and cell division. In contrast, a peptide hormone could not enter the cell and instead bound to receptors on the cell surface, triggering a cascade of intracellular signals through secondary messengers.
(a) Explain why steroid hormones can directly regulate gene expression inside the nucleus.
(b) What is meant by indirect signal transduction in cells?
(c) Describe how signal transduction pathways can influence progression of the cell cycle and cell division.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Analysis, (b) Understanding, (c) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Steroid hormones are lipid-soluble and can cross the plasma membrane to directly activate genes inside the nucleus. (b) Indirect signal transduction occurs when hormones bind to surface receptors and act through secondary messengers inside the cell. (c) Signal transduction pathways regulate proteins and genes that control cell growth and cell division.

questions.text:
Marium is initiating a culture of bacterial cells. She needs a few technical information regarding the exact procedure. Help her by answering the following questions.
(a) Suggest the best method to sterilise glassware, such as pipettes, petri plates, flasks and beakers.
(b) She has prepared coconut milk. Suggest how she can sterilise it.
(c) What would be an ideal source of sugar in a microbial culture medium? Justify your answer.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Application, (b) Application, (c) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Glassware such as pipettes, petri plates, flasks, and beakers are best sterilised using a hot air oven. (b) Coconut milk can be sterilised by membrane filtration. (c) Sucrose is an ideal sugar source because it is easily utilised by microorganisms as an energy source for growth.

questions.text:
Amandeep and Simran are working with pancreatic cell culture. Amandeep uses a haemocytometer, and Simran uses FACS for initial cell sorting and counting.
(a) Whose observations are likely to be error free? Give reason to support your answer.
(b) If a cell is tagged with fluorescent antibody, how will FACS identify it?
(c) How can Simran modify the FACS experiment to count all the three types of pancreatic cells?
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Evaluate, (b) Application, (c) Create; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Simran’s FACS results are more accurate as it is automated and reduces human error. (b) The fluorescent antibody emits light when hit by a laser, and detectors identify the tagged cell. (c) Simran can use different fluorescent antibodies with different colours for each pancreatic cell type. FACS will detect and count them separately.

questions.text:
A biotechnology company developed a genetically modified (GM) mustard plant carrying a Bt gene to protect it against insect pests and improve crop productivity. Before commercial cultivation, the crop was sent to the appropriate regulatory authority in India for biosafety assessment. During evaluation, scientists discussed the possible advantages of the crop as well as concerns regarding its environmental impact, gene flow, and effects on non-target organisms.
(a) Identify the regulatory body responsible for evaluating and approving genetically modified crops in India before their commercial release.
(b) Discuss any two possible environmental risks associated with the large-scale cultivation of genetically modified crops.
(c) Elaborate the importance of implementing biosafety measures before releasing GM crops into the environment.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Recall, (b) Application, (c) Evaluate; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The regulatory body is the Genetic Engineering Appraisal (Approval) Committee (GEAC). (b) GM crops may cause gene flow to wild plants and may affect non-target organisms like beneficial insects. (c) Biosafety measures help ensure that GM crops do not harm the environment, biodiversity, or human health before release.

questions.text:
India is one of the most populous countries in the world, with a population of over 1.4 billion. However, nearly 10 – 15% of couples face infertility problems and seek medical intervention. With advances in medical biotechnology, techniques such as In vitro fertilisation (IVF), embryo transfer, stem cell research, and cryopreservation have transformed reproductive medicine. Along with scientific progress, questions related to ethics, law, and societal impact have become increasingly important in the regulation and application of these technologies.
(a) Discuss one Ethical and one Legal issue of IVF technology.
(b) Explain one property of stem cells that make them medically useful.
(c) How is cryopreservation useful in IVF?
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Evaluate, (b) Understanding, (c) Application; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Ethical issue: Disposal or misuse of unused embryos. Legal issue: Regulation of donor identity and parental rights. (b) Stem cells can differentiate into different cell types, making them useful for tissue repair and therapy. (c) Cryopreservation helps store embryos, sperms, or eggs at very low temperatures for future IVF use.

questions.text:
A young girl named Meena is brought to a clinic for evaluation of short stature and lack of secondary sexual characteristics. Karyotype analysis shows absence of one sex chromosome.
(a) Identify the disorder and its chromosomal condition.
(b) Explain the mechanism responsible for this abnormality during meiosis.
(c) Analyse how this condition affects growth and reproductive development.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Understanding, (b) Understanding, (c) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The disorder is Turner syndrome caused by monosomy X (45, XO). (b) The abnormality occurs due to nondisjunction during meiosis, where sex chromosomes fail to separate properly. (c) It causes short stature, underdeveloped ovaries, and lack of secondary sexual characteristics, leading to infertility.

questions.text:
After a kidney transplant operation, the patient’s immune system began attacking the transplanted organ. Doctors explained that the immune cells recognised the donated organ as foreign tissue.
(a) Which molecules are mainly responsible for tissue compatibility?
(b) Why does organ rejection occur?
(c) Explain the role of T-lymphocytes in this rejection process.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Recall, (b) Understanding, (c) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) molecules, also called Human Leukocyte-associated Antigens (HLA) in humans. (b) Organ rejection occurs when the recipient's immune system recognizes the HLA/MHC molecules of donor’s organ as foreign and mounts an immune response against it. (c) T-lymphocytes recognize the foreign HLA/MHC antigens on the transplanted organ and activate a cell-mediated immune response, leading to the destruction of the transplanted tissue.

questions.text:
Chitin and cellulose are structurally similar polysaccharides, yet they differ significantly in biological function and enzymatic digestibility.
Answer the following:
(a) Identify the monomeric unit present in chitin.
(b) Explain why chitin exhibits greater rigidity than cellulose.
(c) Analyse why cellulase cannot efficiently digest chitin.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Recall, (b) Understanding, (c) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The monomeric unit of Chitin is N-acetyl glucosamine. (b) Chitin is more rigid due to the presence of nitrogen-containing acetyl amino groups that increase hydrogen bonding. (c) Cellulase cannot digest chitin efficiently because chitin has different chemical bonds and monomer units than cellulose.

questions.text:
Observe the following graph showing the activity of different enzymes at various pH values. The graph indicates that each enzyme functions best at a particular optimum pH, beyond which its activity decreases rapidly. For example, pepsin works efficiently in acidic conditions, while pancreatic amylase functions best in alkaline medium.
(a) Why does enzyme activity decrease sharply away from the optimum pH?
(b) Explain how changes in pH affect protein structure.
(c) Predict what would happen if pepsin is transferred to an alkaline medium.
extractionIssues: Graph on page 26 (enzyme activity against pH) not reproduced (its key features are described in the text)
Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Understanding, (b) Analysis, (c) Application; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Enzyme activity decreases away from optimum pH because changes in pH alter the active site of the enzyme. (b) Changes in pH disrupt ionic and hydrogen bonds, altering the protein’s three-dimensional structure. (c) In an alkaline medium, pepsin becomes inactive or denatured and cannot digest proteins effectively.

questions.text:
During a practical class in biotechnology, a student named Rizwan performed paper chromatography to separate different plant pigments extracted from leaves. In this technique, a drop of pigment extract is placed near the base of a strip of chromatography paper, and the lower end of the paper is dipped into a suitable solvent. As the solvent rises upward through the paper by capillary action, different pigments move at different rates depending on their solubility in the solvent and their attraction toward the paper. After the experiment, Rizwan observed that the solvent front had travelled 12 cm from the origin and the paper showed different colours. Observe the figure carefully and answer the questions that follow:
(a) Calculate the Rf value for all the pigments.
(b) Based on these values, which pigment has the highest affinity for the mobile phase?
(c) Why does the cellulose paper act as a polar stationary phase even though it is a solid?
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Application, (b) Analysis, (c) Understanding; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Rf value = Distance travelled by pigment / Distance travelled by solvent • Carotene = 11.4 / 12 = 0.95 • Xanthophyll = 8.4 / 12 = 0.70 • Chlorophyll a = 7.8 / 12 = 0.65 • Chlorophyll b = 5.4 / 12 = 0.45 (b) Carotene has the highest affinity for the mobile phase because it has the highest Rf value. (c) Cellulose paper acts as a polar stationary phase because it contains many hydroxyl (–OH) groups that attract polar molecules.

questions.text:
A culture of liver cells was maintained in a laboratory for several weeks. When nutrients became insufficient, the cells stopped dividing and entered a resting condition, although they continued performing normal metabolic activities. Once nutrients and growth factors were supplied again, the cells resumed the cell cycle and started dividing actively.
(a) Name the phase into which these cells entered during nutrient deficiency.
(b) Why are such cells considered metabolically active despite not dividing?
(c) Which phase of the cell cycle is considered most variable in duration and why?
(d) Explain how external environmental factors can regulate progression of the cell cycle.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Recall, (b) Understanding, (c) Analysis, (d) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The cells entered the G₀ (quiescent) phase. (b) They are metabolically active because they continue respiration, protein synthesis, and other vital functions. (c) The G₁ phase is most variable because its duration depends on cell type and environmental conditions. (d) Factors like nutrients, growth factors, temperature, and toxins can stimulate or inhibit progression of the cell cycle.

questions.text:
Plants produce certain chemical compounds called secondary metabolites which mainly help in defence and protection. Quinine and nicotine are alkaloids, curcumin and tannins are phenolics, gossypol and phaseolin are phytoalexins, while taxol is a terpenoid with medicinal importance.
Answer the following questions:
(a) Name the category of secondary metabolites to which quinine and nicotine belong. Why are they called secondary metabolites?
(b) Curcumin and tannins belong to which category of secondary metabolites? Mention one role of these compounds in plants.
(c) Name the category of compounds to which gossypol and phaseolin belong. Why are these compounds produced in plants?
(d) Taxol belongs to which category of secondary metabolites? Why is it considered important?

officialAnswer.text: (a) Quinine and nicotine belong to the category alkaloids. They are called secondary metabolites because they are not directly involved in the normal growth, development, or reproduction of plants, but help in defence, protection, and survival. (b) Curcumin and tannins belong to the category phenolics. One role of these compounds in plants is protection against pathogens and herbivores. (c) Gossypol and phaseolin belong to the category phytoalexins. These compounds are produced in plants as a defence response against pathogen attack or stress conditions. (d) Taxol belongs to the category terpenoids. It is considered important because it is an anticancer drug used in the treatment of cancer.

questions.text:
At a diagnostic laboratory, two microbiologists, Dr. Mala and Dr. Arther, are investigating blood samples collected from patients suspected of suffering from a newly spreading viral infection. Dr. Meera performs a diagnostic assay as shown in figure given below. The wells of a microtiter plate are first coated with virus-specific antibodies. The serum sample from patient Rahul, containing component (P), is then added into the wells. After washing, enzyme-linked secondary antibodies are introduced, followed by addition of substrate (S), which produces a colour change in positive samples.
During the experiment, Rahul’s sample develops a strong yellow colour, whereas another patient, Sneha, shows no colour development even after addition of substrate (S). Dr. Arther explains that the test depends on highly specific antigen–antibody interactions and enzyme-mediated detection.
Based on the above information and figure, answer the following questions:
(a) Explain why technique used by Dr. Mala is considered highly specific for detecting viral infections.
(b) What does component (P) present in Rahul’s serum most likely represent?
(c) Sneha’s sample failed to produce any colour change after addition of substrate (S). Give two possible scientific explanations for this observation.
(d) If the washing step between addition of serum and enzyme-linked antibodies was skipped accidentally then how this would affect the reliability of the test result and justify your answer.
extractionIssues: Figure on page 29 (ELISA assay steps) not reproduced (the procedure is described in the text)
As printed, the stem names Dr. Mala, Dr. Arther and Dr. Meera
Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Understanding, (b) Analysis, (c) Evaluate, (d) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) ELISA is highly specific because it uses specific antigen–antibody binding and enzyme-based colour detection. (b) Component (P) most likely represents the viral antigen or specific antibody. (c) Viral antigen/antibody absent in Sneha’s serum. Enzyme-linked antibody or reagent failed to work properly. (d) Skipping washing leaves unbound molecules in the wells, causing non-specific colour development and false positive results.

questions.text:
While studying protein chemistry in a biochemistry laboratory, a researcher isolated an unknown polypeptide and treated it with 1-fluoro-2,4-dinitrobenzene (FDNB), also known as Sanger’s reagent, under alkaline conditions. After the reaction, a stable, yellow-coloured compound was formed. The researcher then hydrolysed the polypeptide and analysed the labelled amino acid to determine the amino acid present at one end of the protein chain. This experiment was part of an attempt to study the amino acid sequence and structure of the polypeptide.
Answer the following:
(a) Identify the biochemical technique illustrated in this reaction.
(b) Analyse the chemical principle responsible for the formation of the yellow derivative.
(c) Explain how this method helps identify the N-terminal amino acid of a polypeptide.
(d) Suggest one limitation of this technique and name one alternative method used for protein sequencing.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Recall, (b) Analysis, (c) Understanding, (d) Evaluate; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The technique is Sanger’s method for N-terminal amino acid identification. (b) FDNB reacts with the free alpha-amino group at the N-terminus under alkaline conditions, forming a stable yellow dinitrophenyl (DNP) derivative. (c) After acid hydrolysis, only the DNP-labelled N-terminal amino acid remains intact and is identified by chromatography. (d) Limitation: It identifies only the N-terminal amino acid, not the complete sequence. Alternative method: Edman degradation.

questions.text:
During a developmental biology workshop, students observed images of human embryos at different stages of development. In the early stages, the hands and feet appeared as paddle-like structures. Later, the tissues between the developing fingers and toes gradually disappeared, resulting in the formation of separate digits. Researchers explained that this occurs through a genetically controlled mechanism that removes unwanted cells without damaging surrounding tissues. Another scientist compared this process with necrosis, where cells die due to injury and release harmful substances into nearby tissues.
(a) Name the process responsible for the removal of unnecessary cells during development.
(b) Which group of enzymes mainly regulates this process?
(c) Differentiate between apoptosis and necrosis with respect to cellular damage and physiological significance.
(d) Predict one possible consequence if apoptosis does not occur properly in the human body.
extractionIssues: Table in the official answer (page 41) flattened row by row with ' | '
Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Understanding, (b) Analysis, (c) Application, (d) Evaluate; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The process is called apoptosis (programmed cell death). (b) The process is mainly regulated by caspases (proteolytic enzymes). (c) Apoptosis | Necrosis; Controlled and programmed cell death | Uncontrolled cell death due to injury; Does not damage nearby cells | Damages surrounding tissues; Important for normal development and tissue maintenance | Causes inflammation and tissue damage (d) Failure of apoptosis may lead to cancer due to uncontrolled cell growth.

questions.text:
While working in the plant biotechnology laboratory, Ritu was assigned the task of preparing a nutrient medium for culturing carrot explants. Before pouring the medium into culture bottles, she carefully added auxin and cytokinin in specific proportions as instructed by her teacher. She observed that different combinations of these hormones produced different patterns of growth in the cultured tissues.
(a) What is most likely to happen in the culture if the concentration of auxin is much higher than cytokinin?
(b) Why different combinations of auxin and cytokinin produce different growth responses in plant tissue cultures?
(c) Mention the importance of maintaining the correct hormone ratio while preparing a plant tissue culture medium.
(d) Suggest a suitable hormone combination strategy to obtain shoot formation from carrot explants in culture.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Application, (b) Analysis, (c) Evaluate, (d) Create; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) If auxin concentration is much higher than cytokinin, root formation will occur. (b) Auxin and cytokinin regulate cell division and differentiation differently, so their ratio determines whether roots, shoots, or callus develop. (c) Maintaining the correct hormone ratio ensures the desired growth and proper development of cultured tissues. (d) For shoot formation, the medium should contain higher cytokinin and lower auxin concentration.

questions.text:
David was performing an experiment to study the effect of temperature, pH, and substrate concentration on the activity of enzyme diastase. He took 5 mL of starch solution in a test tube and added 2 mL of diastase. The mixture was incubated under optimal conditions for the enzyme. Gradually, the starch concentration was increased up to 50 mL and the temperature was increased to 80°C.
(a) Explain the effect of increasing starch concentration on the activity of diastase and explain why the reaction rate does not continue to increase indefinitely.
(b) Predict the effect of raising the temperature to 80°C on the structure and activity of diastase. Give a scientific reason for your answer.
(c) Explain why enzymes show maximum activity only at a particular pH and temperature.
(d) Discuss the importance of maintaining optimum conditions for enzyme activity in industrial and biological processes.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Analysis, (b) Application, (c) Understanding, (d) Evaluate; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Enzyme activity increases with starch concentration until all active sites of diastase become saturated, after which the reaction rate remains constant. (b) At 80°C, diastase gets denatured, so its active site changes shape and enzyme activity is lost. (c) Enzymes show maximum activity only at a particular pH and temperature because their active site functions best under optimum conditions. (d) Maintaining optimum conditions ensures maximum enzyme efficiency in biological and industrial processes.

questions.text:
Dr. Mariya, a medical geneticist, was studying patients affected by inherited metabolic disorders caused by enzyme deficiencies or mutations affecting protein structure. One patient showed very little skin pigmentation, another had high phenylalanine levels in the blood, a third showed accumulation of dark pigments in connective tissues, while another suffered from abnormal haemoglobin leading to reduced oxygen transport. Dr. Mariya explained that early diagnosis of such disorders is essential for proper treatment and management.
(a) Analyse the biochemical defect responsible for reduced melanin synthesis and identify the disorder associated with it.
(b) Identify the disorder caused by deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) and explain its effect on normal metabolism.
(c) Name the disorder caused by accumulation of homogentisic acid in connective tissues and evaluate its effect on the body.
(d) Explain how substitution of valine in place of glutamic acid in haemoglobin affects its structure and function. Name the disorder associated with this mutation.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Analysis, (b) Understanding, (c) Evaluate, (d) Application; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Reduced melanin synthesis is caused by deficiency of tyrosinase enzyme and the disorder is albinism. (b) Deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase causes phenylketonuria (PKU), leading to accumulation of phenylalanine in the body. (c) Accumulation of homogentisic acid causes alkaptonuria, which leads to dark pigmentation of connective tissues and joint problems. (d) Replacement of glutamic acid by valine changes the structure of haemoglobin, reducing oxygen transport efficiency; the disorder is sickle-cell anaemia.

questions.text:
A biotechnology company headed by Dr. Ratna develops a recombinant drug for treatment of a rare genetic disorder after years of research. The company patents the product and sells it at a very high cost. Patient groups begin protesting because many affected individuals cannot afford the medicine.
(a) Why would the company prefer patent protection instead of keeping the process public?
(b) How does patent protection encourage further biotechnological research?
(c) Analyse one social problem that may arise due to high pricing of patented drugs.
(d) Suggest one ethical measure by which the government can improve public access to such medicines.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Application, (b) Analysis, (c) Analysis, (d) Evaluate; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) The company prefers patent protection to prevent others from copying the product and to recover research and development costs. (b) Patent protection encourages biotechnology research by providing financial rewards and exclusive rights to inventors. (c) High pricing of patented drugs may create inequality, where poor patients cannot access life-saving medicines. (d) The government can improve access by providing subsidies or allowing production of low-cost generic medicines.

questions.text:
In an animal tissue culture laboratory, researchers prepared DMEM medium for mammalian cells. However, the cultured cells stopped growing after two days. Investigation revealed improper sterilisation and incorrect handling of vitamins and enzymes added to the medium.
(a) Why must vitamins and enzymes be handled carefully during media preparation?
(b) Analyse how improper sterilisation can affect animal cell cultures.
(c) Why are transfer areas sterilised before inoculation procedures?
(d) Suggest one suitable method for sterilising heat-sensitive components of culture media.
extractionIssues: Parts carry different printed tags: (a) Application, (b) Analysis, (c) Application, (d) Analysis; no single cognitiveLevel recorded.

officialAnswer.text: (a) Vitamins and enzymes must be handled carefully because they are heat-sensitive and may lose activity if damaged. (b) Improper sterilisation can cause contamination by microorganisms, which compete with or destroy animal cells. (c) Transfer areas are sterilised to prevent contamination during inoculation procedures. (d) Membrane filtration is a suitable method for sterilising heat-sensitive components of culture media.
